title: Energy from fuels
source: Questions and terms copied unchanged from the site's bank, except where marked for IB Diploma Chemistry (status of the source: ai-reviewed-reverified-gate-verified-2026-09-30-awaiting-human-signoff). Terms and clues: R1.3.3#xt1 term and clue written for the game; R1.3.2#xt1 term and clue written for the game; R1.3#c16 bank term, clue written for the game from the bank's definition; R1.3.4#xt1 term and clue written for the game. Questions: R1.3#q09, R1.3#q11, R1.3#q10, R1.3#q12, R1.3#q13, R1.3#q16.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Fossil fuels
items.clue: Coal, crude oil and natural gas: non-renewable energy sources.

items.label: Incomplete combustion
items.clue: Burning in a limited supply of oxygen, forming carbon monoxide or soot.

items.label: Fuel cell
items.clue: Converts chemical energy from a continuously supplied reactant directly into electricity.

items.label: Biofuel
items.clue: Renewable energy source made from recently living biomass, such as ethanol from sugar cane.

questions.stem: Biofuels are renewable energy sources, whereas fossil fuels are non-renewable. Which statement gives the defining feature of a renewable energy source?

options.text: It can be collected and used again after it has released its energy.
It adds no carbon dioxide to the atmosphere overall when used.
It comes from a natural source, such as the remains of plants or animals.
It is replenished naturally at least as fast as it is used.

questions.explanation: Renewable is about the rate of replacement: new crops for biofuels grow within months or years, whereas coal, oil and gas took millions of years to form and are used far faster than they form.

questions.stem: In a hydrogen fuel cell with an acidic electrolyte, hydrogen gas is supplied to the anode. Which half-equation represents the reaction at the anode?

options.text: H₂ → 2H⁺ + 2e⁻
2H⁺ + 2e⁻ → H₂
H₂ + 2e⁻ → 2H⁻

questions.explanation: Oxidation takes place at the anode: each hydrogen molecule loses two electrons, forming two H⁺ ions that move through the acidic electrolyte to the cathode. The electrons flow through the external circuit.

questions.stem: Bioethanol is made by fermenting sugar from sugar cane and is burned as a fuel for vehicles. Which statement about bioethanol as a fuel is correct?

options.text: It burns to form water only, so using it as a fuel adds no CO₂ to the atmosphere.
The CO₂ it releases is exactly balanced by photosynthesis, so its net emission is zero.
All of its carbon was fixed from atmospheric CO₂ by photosynthesis in the cane.
Its carbon was taken from the soil by the roots of the cane, not from CO₂ in the air.

questions.stem: In a methanol fuel cell with an acidic electrolyte, an aqueous solution of methanol is supplied to the anode. Which equation represents the reaction that occurs at the anode?

options.text: 2CH₃OH(aq) + O₂(g) → 2CO₂(g) + 8H⁺(aq) + 8e⁻
CH₃OH(aq) + H₂O(l) → CO₂(g) + 6H⁺(aq) + 6e⁻
2CH₃OH(aq) + 3O₂(g) → 2CO₂(g) + 4H₂O(l)
CO₂(g) + 6H⁺(aq) + 6e⁻ → CH₃OH(l) + H₂O(l)

questions.explanation: Methanol is oxidized at the anode. Water supplies the second O atom needed for CO₂; balancing H gives 6H⁺ (4 from CH₃OH, 2 from H₂O), and balancing charge gives 6e⁻. The electrons flow to the cathode through the external circuit.

questions.stem: Plants such as sugar cane, grown to make bioethanol, carry out photosynthesis. Which statement gives the reactants and products of photosynthesis?

options.text: Glucose reacts with oxygen to form carbon dioxide and water.
Water and soil minerals react to form glucose and oxygen.
Carbon dioxide and water react to form glucose and oxygen gas.
Carbon dioxide reacts to form carbon and oxygen gas.

questions.explanation: Photosynthesis uses light energy to convert carbon dioxide and water into glucose and oxygen: 6CO₂(g) + 6H₂O(l) → C₆H₁₂O₆(aq) + 6O₂(g). The carbon in glucose, and so in a biofuel made from it, comes from atmospheric CO₂.

questions.stem: In a hydrogen fuel cell with an acidic electrolyte, which equation represents the reaction that occurs at the cathode?

options.text: 4H₂O(l) → 2O₂(g) + 8H⁺(aq) + 8e⁻
O(g) + 2H⁺(aq) + 2e⁻ → H₂O(l)
H₂(g) + ½O₂(g) → H₂O(l) + heat
O₂(g) + 4H⁺(aq) + 4e⁻ → 2H₂O(l)

questions.explanation: Reduction takes place at the cathode: each O₂ molecule gains four electrons and, with four H⁺ ions from the acidic electrolyte, forms two water molecules. O, H and charge all balance.
